sharedRules.name: Transitus Instantaneus
sharedRules.description:
If Lord Commander Varian is joined to and leading a unit with the Lion’s Blade Trait, that unit may enter the battlefield using Deep Strike. When the unit would arrive from Deep Strike, Lord Commander Varian must make an Intelligence Check with a -2 modifier.

If the Check is passed, the unit enters the battlefield normally.

If the Check is failed, the unit does not enter the battlefield and remains in Reserves. The unit immediately suffers D3 Mortal Wounds. These Mortal Wounds cannot be prevented, ignored, reduced or otherwise modified in any way. The controlling player may allocate these Mortal Wounds amongst models in the unit.

Lord Commander Varian must always be the model that makes this Intelligence Check.

sharedRules.name: Oathbound Bulwark
sharedRules.description: This Special Reaction may be declared when a Unit that includes one or more Praesides Spei Models and one or more friendly Character Models is selected as the target of an attack. The Controlling Player must expend 1 Reaction Point to make this Reaction. Until that attack has been completely resolved, the enemy Player cannot select any Character Model in this Unit as the Target Model by means of the Precision (X) Special Rule, or by means of any other Special Rule, Wargear or effect that would normally allow the Attacking Player to choose the Target Model. Hits and Wounds are allocated using the normal rules instead. This Reaction cannot be declared if there are no non-Character Praesides Spei Models remaining in the Unit.

rules.name: The Blade of Resolve
rules.description:
"Models with this Special Rule gain a bonus when Locked in Combat with Units which have Tactical Statuses."
When Locked in Combat with any Units which contain at least one Model which has any Tactical Statuses, Models in that Combat with this Special Rule gain an additional modifier of +1 to their Attacks Characteristic until the end of the Phase.

rules.name: The Unbroken Blade
rules.description:
When a Unit composed entirely of Models with the Lion’s Blade Trait makes a Disordered Charge, that Unit may still make a Set-up Move and Volley Attacks as though the Charge was not Disordered.

The Charge is still considered Disordered for all other purposes, and Models in that Unit may not gain any benefit from Special Rules that require them to have successfully Charged.

characteristics.name: Summary
characteristics.$text: This Gambit grants a greater Focus bonus when facing an opponent with equal or higher Weapon Skill.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This Gambit can only be selected during the first Face-Off Step of a Challenge involving this Model. When resolving the Focus Step, compare the Base Weapon Skill Characteristic of this Model and the opposing Model. If the opposing Model has a higher Base Weapon Skill Characteristic, add +2 to this Model’s Focus Roll. If the opposing Model has an equal Base Weapon Skill Characteristic, add +1 instead. If the opposing Model has a lower Base Weapon Skill Characteristic, this Gambit provides no modifier.

characteristics.name: Summary
characteristics.$text: A Lion’s Blade Unit may attempt an emergency teleport when targeted by a Shooting Attack, but repeated use rapidly destabilises the teleportation matrix.

characteristics.name: Trigger
characteristics.$text: The Reactive Player may declare the Transitus Ultima Advanced Reaction when the Active Player declares a Shooting Attack that targets a Unit under the Reactive Player’s control which only includes Models with the Lion’s Blade Trait and does not include any Models with the Vehicle Type. This Advanced Reaction may be declared a maximum of three times during the battle. The number of times it has been declared is tracked across the entire Army.

characteristics.name: Cost
characteristics.$text: The Reactive Player must spend 1 point of their Reaction Allowance each time Transitus Ultima is declared.

characteristics.name: Target
characteristics.$text: The Target Unit is always the Unit targeted by the Shooting Attack that triggered this Reaction. That Unit is the Reacting Unit.

characteristics.name: Process
characteristics.$text:
1. Immediately make an Intelligence Check for the Reacting Unit. On the first use of Transitus Ultima, this Check is made with a -1 modifier; on the second use, with a -3 modifier; and on the third use, with a -5 modifier. After the third use, Transitus Ultima may not be declared again for the remainder of the battle.
2. If the Check is passed, every Model in the Reacting Unit may be repositioned up to 6" from its current position. Models may move through other Models and Terrain while making this move, but must end the move in Unit Coherency, more than 1" away from all enemy Models, and may not be placed within Impassable Terrain.
3. After this repositioning has been resolved, the Active Player continues resolving the Shooting Attack normally. If the Reacting Unit is no longer an eligible Target due to Range or Line of Sight, the Shooting Attack ends and the Attacking Unit may not select a new Target.
4. If the Intelligence Check is failed, the Reacting Unit is not moved and immediately suffers D3 Wounds. No Saving Throws or Damage Mitigation Tests may be made against these Wounds. The Shooting Attack then continues normally.
